title: An elementary counterexample to Long’s clique equality

initial.assessment: Complete TeX and all PDF pages inspected, including the source convention of prime element. Quotient norm, nonprincipality via mod5, nonzero prime maximality, and sharp coloring mechanism reconstructed.

proof: A rational trace-and-norm argument shows the full ring of integers is Z[√10]: after denominator bound v²|40, mod4 excludes odd coefficient numerators. Multiplication determinant gives the principal ideal norm. Reduction of constant term modulo two has kernel P=(2,√10).

If P were principal, norm equation a²−10b²=±2 would give a nonsquare modulo five. The index formula also shows every nonzero prime ideal quotient is a finite integral domain and hence a field. No prime element can therefore lie in this nonprincipal prime ideal. Same-color differences contain neither primes nor units. The edge from 0 to 1 attains 2 in both graphs, so equality fails as 2 versus 4.

Nonzero ideal minimization includes P and norm lower bound two. The zero ideal gives an infinite quotient. Irreducible 2 or the inclusion of higher powers P²=(2) would create a triangle; those conventions are distinct.
